Types of Health Insurance Policies for Individuals and Families by Bajaj General Insurance
We understand that everyone’s health needs are different, and so are the insurance options. The right plan depends on your age, family size, medical history, and budget. With Bajaj General Insurance Limited, you can choose from a variety of health insurance plans that make sense for you and your loved ones.
Let’s look at the types of health insurance plans we offer, and which one best suits you:

sections.heading: Family Floater Health Insurance
sections.text:
Instead of buying separate policies, you can cover your whole family under one plan with a shared sum insured. It usually works out more cost-effectively, especially when family members are younger.
The premium is based on the eldest person in the family, so if you include parents, it’s a good idea to go for a higher sum insured.

sections.heading: regular health check-ups
sections.text: Since terms like room rent limits or co-pay clauses can apply, it’s important to review them carefully.

sections.heading: Super Top-Up Health Insurance
sections.text:
This plan adds an extra layer of protection on top of your base policy. It starts covering once your medical bills cross a fixed amount (deductible). For example, if your deductible is ₹5 lakh and your hospital bill is ₹8 lakh, the super top-up will pay the remaining ₹3 lakh.
It’s a smart way to get more extensive coverage, like ₹25 lakh or ₹50 lakh, without paying a very high premium.

sections.heading: Maternity Cover Insurance
sections.text:
Are you thinking of planning a family? Maternity insurance cushions you against soaring hospital bills, covering expenses for both normal and C-section deliveries. Crucially, many plans also extend coverage to your newborn from day one, including vaccinations.
The catch is the waiting period, which is often 2 to 4 years. Therefore, buy this before you plan to conceive.
Buy the best health insurance plans in India from Bajaj General Insurance and get exciting discounts and benefits!

Now that we know the differences, the question remains: which one should you choose? The choice boils down to a balance between cost and security.
If you are under 40 with a young family, a family floater plan with a super top-up is typically the financially savvy choice.
However, never include senior citizen parents in a floater plan; their higher age will spike your premium, and their frequent health needs will drain the family’s coverage. Always buy them a separate individual policy.

sections.heading: Real-Life Scenarios: How Health Insurance Actually Works?
sections.text:
Okay, enough technical talk. We all know that health insurance plans help you financially during medical emergencies. But how does that translate into real life? Let’s understand below.
Meet Rahul, a 28-year-old graphic designer in Pune. He always felt he was ‘
too young
’ for insurance but bought a basic plan just for tax savings. One Tuesday night, he woke up with severe abdominal pain, which the doctors diagnosed as acute appendicitis.

sections.heading: 1. What Happened Next
sections.text: : His flatmate rushed him to a nearby hospital. Since this hospital was in his insurer’s network of hospitals, Rahul didn't have to panic about the deposit money. He simply showed his health card at the TPA desk.

sections.heading: 2. The Bill
sections.text: : The total cost of surgery and a 3-day stay is ₹85,000.

sections.heading: The Inflation Trap
sections.text:
The cost of healthcare in India is rising at double the rate of general inflation. In fact, medical inflation is at 12-14%, while general retail inflation is at 0.7% YoY in November 2025.
This means a surgery that cost ₹3 lakh just a few years ago could now easily exceed ₹5 lakh. Without an active health insurance plan, this double-digit inflation directly drains your hard-earned savings, making quality healthcare unaffordable.

sections.heading: Lower Premiums
sections.text: Insurers calculate premiums based on risk, which is lowest when you are young. Because Arjun is 25, his premium is minimal. By purchasing now, he locks in a cost-effective rate. If he waits until he is older, the premium for the same coverage will be significantly higher.

sections.heading: Comprehensive Coverage
sections.text: Since Arjun has no pre-existing conditions (like hypertension or diabetes), he doesn't have to worry about exclusions. He gets comprehensive coverage immediately. If he waits and develops a lifestyle condition later, the insurer might apply a long waiting period or permanently exclude that condition from the policy.

sections.heading: The Financial Shock of Managing Health
sections.text: The real burden is physical as well as financial. Lifestyle diseases aren't usually ‘cure once and move on’ events. Instead, they are recurring costs which can quickly drain your entire savings.

sections.heading: Heart Health:
sections.text: A standard angioplasty in a private metro hospital now costs between ₹1.5 lakh and ₹3.5 lakh. If open-heart surgery is needed, the bill easily exceeds ₹5 lakh.

sections.heading: Cost and Benefit Related Factors
sections.text: One of the first things that comes to mind when thinking about health insurance is the premium cost and the benefits it will provide. Here are a few things you should consider:

sections.heading: 1. Premium Amount
sections.text: : Your first step is to compare different premium amounts from different policies. It will help you choose the most suitable for your budget.

sections.heading: 2. Co-Payment
sections.text: : Before buying a policy, always check if there are any co-payment clauses. Although they can reduce your premium, they can also increase your out-of-pocket payments.

sections.heading: 3. Sum Insured Amount
sections.text: : Always compare the premium and the sum insured amount before you commit to a policy. This will ensure that you get adequate coverage for you and your family.

sections.heading: Opt for a Higher Deductible
sections.text:
One of the simplest ways to reduce your health insurance premium is by opting for a higher deductible. A deductible is the amount you pay out-of-pocket before your insurance coverage kicks in.
By choosing a higher deductible, you can significantly lower your premium because the insurer's risk is reduced. However, it’s important to ensure that the deductible amount is manageable for you in case of a medical emergency.
This approach is suitable for individuals who are generally healthy and do not anticipate incurring frequent medical expenses.

sections.heading: Health Insurance Tax Benefits
sections.text: Health insurance not only helps you manage unexpected medical expenses but also offers significant tax benefits under the Income Tax Act, 1961. By paying premiums for your health insurance plan, you can reduce your taxable income and save money while ensuring your family is protected.

sections.heading: Key Benefits:
sections.text:
1. Premium Deduction for Self, Spouse, and Children: You can claim a deduction of up to ₹25,000 for premiums paid for yourself, your spouse, and dependent children.
2. Additional Deduction for Parents: If your parents are below 60 years, you can claim up to ₹25,000. For senior citizen parents (above 60 years), the deduction increases to ₹50,000.
3. Maximum Deduction: You can claim up to ₹1,00,000 as a deduction under Section 80D, but this maximum applies only when both you (the taxpayer) and your parents are senior citizens, allowing ₹50,000 each. For most individuals below 60, the practical upper limit is ₹75,000 - ₹25,000 for self/family and ₹50,000 for senior-citizen parents.
4. Preventive Health Check-Ups: Costs for preventive health check-ups are also included within the limits, up to ₹5,000 per year.
5. Payment Mode: Premiums must be paid via non-cash methods like debit/credit cards, net banking, or UPI to be eligible for tax deduction.

Suppose you pay a premium of ₹20,000 for your own family (self, spouse, and children) and ₹30,000 for your senior citizen parents. Here’s how the deduction works:

sections.text: 3. Total Deduction: ₹20,000 + ₹30,000 = ₹50,000 deducted from taxable income.

sections.heading: GST Update:
sections.text: As of 22 September 2025, GST on individual and family health insurance premiums has effectively been made 0% (no 18% GST) under the latest GST reform, though this does not change the 80D deduction amounts; it simply reduces the out‑of‑pocket premium cost.

sections.heading: Sum Insured
sections.text:
The sum insured is the maximum amount that the insurer will pay for your medical expenses during a policy year. It is the coverage limit of your health insurance policy.
Choosing an adequate sum insured ensures that you have sufficient coverage to meet potential medical costs without significant out-of-pocket expenses.

sections.heading: Waiting Period
sections.text:
The waiting period is the amount of time you must wait before certain recruitments kick in. The waiting period may be a few months to a few years, depending on the given policy and the condition.
Most waiting periods relate to pre-existing conditions, maternity benefits, and some specific treatments. Knowing the

sections.heading: waiting period
sections.text: allows you to make decisions about any possible healthcare needs and not encounter surprises when it's time to file a claim.

sections.heading: Premium
sections.text: The premium is the amount you pay on a recurring basis (monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or annually) to maintain your health insurance policy. It varies depending on age, health condition, how much coverage you want, and lifestyle choices.

sections.heading: co-pay
sections.text: , is the percentage of the medical bill that you must pay out-of-pocket while the insurer covers the rest. It helps reduce the premium cost but means you share the cost of treatment.

sections.heading: Deductible
sections.text: A deductible is a fixed amount you need to pay each year before the insurer starts covering the expenses. Higher deductibles generally lead to lower premiums but require you to pay more out-of-pocket initially.

sections.heading: What is the ideal health insurance cover amount I should buy?
sections.text:
Your ideal level of health insurance coverage amount is complete;y subjective! Your age, city, family size, and health requirements all play a role. Given the rising cost of healthcare, families and metro areas should budget at least ₹5–10 lakhs, if not more. You can select customised protection with Bajaj General for total peace of mind!
Can I add my parents to my health insurance policy?
Caring for your parents' health is paramount. With Bajaj General, you can easily add parents to health insurance policies. This ensures they get quality medical care without financial strain. Bajaj General has several add-ons that makes the policy unique to you. Check out our family or senior citizen plans. They offer strong coverage, giving you and your loved ones total peace of mind.

sections.heading: Which diseases are not covered in health insurance?
sections.text: Bajaj General Insurance offers tailored & well-designed policies. Generally,

sections.heading: diseases not covered in health insurance
sections.text: often include pre-existing conditions during initial waiting periods, purely cosmetic treatments, and issues arising from substance abuse or self-inflicted harm. For exact details on diseases not covered in your health insurance policy, refer your specific Bajaj General policy wordings for an exclusion list.

sections.heading: Do health insurance plans cover diagnostic charges like X-ray, ultrasound or MRI?
sections.text: Yes, Bajaj General Insurance plans generally cover diagnostic tests like X-rays, ultrasounds, and MRIs. These are typically included as part of pre-hospitalisation, in-patient, or post-hospitalisation expenses when linked to a covered treatment. Many policies also offer preventive health check-up benefits. For precise details on diagnostic tests covered in health insurance, please refer to your policy wordings for specific terms and conditions.

sections.heading: Is OPD covered in health insurance?
sections.text: Yes,

sections.heading: OPD cover in health insurance
sections.text: is increasingly available in many plans with Bajaj General Insurance. While many traditional plans primarily focus on hospitalisation, we offer solutions, often as an add-on or in specialized policies, to help cover outpatient expenses like doctor consultations, diagnostics, and pharmacies.

sections.heading: What is a waiting period in health insurance and how long is it?
sections.text: A waiting period in health insurance is a specific duration after purchasing your policy during which certain benefits are not yet active. This is a standard practice to manage claims responsibly, particularly for pre-existing or recently diagnosed conditions. Bajaj General Insurance policies typically include various waiting periods, such as an initial period, specific ailment periods, etc. for pre-existing diseases. The actual duration varies by plan & the diesease.

sections.heading: Is AYUSH treatment (Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy) covered in health insurance?
sections.text: Yes, Bajaj General Insurance understands the growing preference for diverse healthcare approaches among Indians. Many of our health plans now cover AYUSH treatments (Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy) when availed as in-patient care at recognised facilities. Coverage details, including specific terms and limits, vary by policy. Please refer to your individual plan policy wordings for comprehensive information.

sections.heading: What is OPD cover in health insurance and do Bajaj General insurance include it?
sections.text: OPD cover in health insurance supports expenses like doctor consultations, diagnostic tests, and medicines without hospitalisation. Bajaj General Insurance understands your everyday health needs. Many of our health plans, including My Health Care Plan, offer comprehensive OPD coverage, sometimes even providing twice the OPD benefits of your premium. This helps you manage routine medical costs efficiently.

sections.heading: Can I cancel my health insurance? If yes, will I get my premium back?
sections.text: Yes, you can cancel your existing health insurance for a refund and consider switching to a reliable insurer like Bajaj General Insurance. During the free-look period, typically 15-30 days from issuing of policy, a near-full premium refund is common. A few deductions for medicals or stamp duty may be made. Post free-look, a pro-rata refund for the unexpired term might be available, as per your current insurer's specific terms.

sections.text: Even though Bajaj General Insurance aims to cover many treatments, getting 100 percent claim for health insurance in India for every medical cost depends on what your plan actually includes. Some policies have Deductibles and co-payments which change how much money you receive. Medical coverage helps lower sudden expenses. Always review your policy documents for knowing the benefits and to understand your complete coverage for out-of-pocket costs.

Types of Health Insurance Policies for Individuals and Families by Bajaj General Insurance
We understand that everyone’s health needs are different, and so are the insurance options. The right plan depends on your age, family size, medical history, and budget. With Bajaj General Insurance Limited, you can choose from a variety of health insurance plans that make sense for you and your loved ones.
Let’s look at the types of health insurance plans we offer, and which one best suits you:

chunks.heading: Family Floater Health Insurance
chunks.text:
Instead of buying separate policies, you can cover your whole family under one plan with a shared sum insured. It usually works out more cost-effectively, especially when family members are younger.
The premium is based on the eldest person in the family, so if you include parents, it’s a good idea to go for a higher sum insured.

chunks.heading: regular health check-ups
chunks.text: Since terms like room rent limits or co-pay clauses can apply, it’s important to review them carefully.

chunks.heading: Super Top-Up Health Insurance
chunks.text:
This plan adds an extra layer of protection on top of your base policy. It starts covering once your medical bills cross a fixed amount (deductible). For example, if your deductible is ₹5 lakh and your hospital bill is ₹8 lakh, the super top-up will pay the remaining ₹3 lakh.
It’s a smart way to get more extensive coverage, like ₹25 lakh or ₹50 lakh, without paying a very high premium.

chunks.heading: Maternity Cover Insurance
chunks.text:
Are you thinking of planning a family? Maternity insurance cushions you against soaring hospital bills, covering expenses for both normal and C-section deliveries. Crucially, many plans also extend coverage to your newborn from day one, including vaccinations.
The catch is the waiting period, which is often 2 to 4 years. Therefore, buy this before you plan to conceive.
Buy the best health insurance plans in India from Bajaj General Insurance and get exciting discounts and benefits!

Now that we know the differences, the question remains: which one should you choose? The choice boils down to a balance between cost and security.
If you are under 40 with a young family, a family floater plan with a super top-up is typically the financially savvy choice.
However, never include senior citizen parents in a floater plan; their higher age will spike your premium, and their frequent health needs will drain the family’s coverage. Always buy them a separate individual policy.

chunks.heading: Real-Life Scenarios: How Health Insurance Actually Works?
chunks.text:
Okay, enough technical talk. We all know that health insurance plans help you financially during medical emergencies. But how does that translate into real life? Let’s understand below.
Meet Rahul, a 28-year-old graphic designer in Pune. He always felt he was ‘
too young
’ for insurance but bought a basic plan just for tax savings. One Tuesday night, he woke up with severe abdominal pain, which the doctors diagnosed as acute appendicitis.

chunks.heading: 1. What Happened Next
chunks.text: : His flatmate rushed him to a nearby hospital. Since this hospital was in his insurer’s network of hospitals, Rahul didn't have to panic about the deposit money. He simply showed his health card at the TPA desk.

chunks.heading: 2. The Bill

chunks.heading: The Inflation Trap
chunks.text:
The cost of healthcare in India is rising at double the rate of general inflation. In fact, medical inflation is at 12-14%, while general retail inflation is at 0.7% YoY in November 2025.
This means a surgery that cost ₹3 lakh just a few years ago could now easily exceed ₹5 lakh. Without an active health insurance plan, this double-digit inflation directly drains your hard-earned savings, making quality healthcare unaffordable.

chunks.heading: Lower Premiums
chunks.text: Insurers calculate premiums based on risk, which is lowest when you are young. Because Arjun is 25, his premium is minimal. By purchasing now, he locks in a cost-effective rate. If he waits until he is older, the premium for the same coverage will be significantly higher.

chunks.heading: Comprehensive Coverage
chunks.text: Since Arjun has no pre-existing conditions (like hypertension or diabetes), he doesn't have to worry about exclusions. He gets comprehensive coverage immediately. If he waits and develops a lifestyle condition later, the insurer might apply a long waiting period or permanently exclude that condition from the policy.

chunks.heading: The Financial Shock of Managing Health
chunks.text: The real burden is physical as well as financial. Lifestyle diseases aren't usually ‘cure once and move on’ events. Instead, they are recurring costs which can quickly drain your entire savings.

chunks.heading: Heart Health:
chunks.text: A standard angioplasty in a private metro hospital now costs between ₹1.5 lakh and ₹3.5 lakh. If open-heart surgery is needed, the bill easily exceeds ₹5 lakh.

chunks.text: One of the first things that comes to mind when thinking about health insurance is the premium cost and the benefits it will provide. Here are a few things you should consider:

chunks.heading: 1. Premium Amount
chunks.text: : Your first step is to compare different premium amounts from different policies. It will help you choose the most suitable for your budget.

chunks.heading: 2. Co-Payment
chunks.text: : Before buying a policy, always check if there are any co-payment clauses. Although they can reduce your premium, they can also increase your out-of-pocket payments.

chunks.heading: 3. Sum Insured Amount
chunks.text: : Always compare the premium and the sum insured amount before you commit to a policy. This will ensure that you get adequate coverage for you and your family.

chunks.heading: Opt for a Higher Deductible
chunks.text:
One of the simplest ways to reduce your health insurance premium is by opting for a higher deductible. A deductible is the amount you pay out-of-pocket before your insurance coverage kicks in.
By choosing a higher deductible, you can significantly lower your premium because the insurer's risk is reduced. However, it’s important to ensure that the deductible amount is manageable for you in case of a medical emergency.
This approach is suitable for individuals who are generally healthy and do not anticipate incurring frequent medical expenses.

chunks.heading: Health Insurance Tax Benefits
chunks.text: Health insurance not only helps you manage unexpected medical expenses but also offers significant tax benefits under the Income Tax Act, 1961. By paying premiums for your health insurance plan, you can reduce your taxable income and save money while ensuring your family is protected.

chunks.heading: Key Benefits:
chunks.text:
1. Premium Deduction for Self, Spouse, and Children: You can claim a deduction of up to ₹25,000 for premiums paid for yourself, your spouse, and dependent children.
2. Additional Deduction for Parents: If your parents are below 60 years, you can claim up to ₹25,000. For senior citizen parents (above 60 years), the deduction increases to ₹50,000.
3. Maximum Deduction: You can claim up to ₹1,00,000 as a deduction under Section 80D, but this maximum applies only when both you (the taxpayer) and your parents are senior citizens, allowing ₹50,000 each. For most individuals below 60, the practical upper limit is ₹75,000 - ₹25,000 for self/family and ₹50,000 for senior-citizen parents.
4. Preventive Health Check-Ups: Costs for preventive health check-ups are also included within the limits, up to ₹5,000 per year.
5. Payment Mode: Premiums must be paid via non-cash methods like debit/credit cards, net banking, or UPI to be eligible for tax deduction.

chunks.heading: Sum Insured
chunks.text:
The sum insured is the maximum amount that the insurer will pay for your medical expenses during a policy year. It is the coverage limit of your health insurance policy.
Choosing an adequate sum insured ensures that you have sufficient coverage to meet potential medical costs without significant out-of-pocket expenses.

chunks.heading: Waiting Period
chunks.text:
The waiting period is the amount of time you must wait before certain recruitments kick in. The waiting period may be a few months to a few years, depending on the given policy and the condition.
Most waiting periods relate to pre-existing conditions, maternity benefits, and some specific treatments. Knowing the

chunks.heading: waiting period
chunks.text: allows you to make decisions about any possible healthcare needs and not encounter surprises when it's time to file a claim.

chunks.heading: Premium
chunks.text: The premium is the amount you pay on a recurring basis (monthly, quarterly, half-yearly, or annually) to maintain your health insurance policy. It varies depending on age, health condition, how much coverage you want, and lifestyle choices.

chunks.heading: co-pay
chunks.text: , is the percentage of the medical bill that you must pay out-of-pocket while the insurer covers the rest. It helps reduce the premium cost but means you share the cost of treatment.

chunks.heading: Deductible
chunks.text: A deductible is a fixed amount you need to pay each year before the insurer starts covering the expenses. Higher deductibles generally lead to lower premiums but require you to pay more out-of-pocket initially.

chunks.heading: What is a waiting period in health insurance and how long is it?
chunks.text: A waiting period in health insurance is a specific duration after purchasing your policy during which certain benefits are not yet active. This is a standard practice to manage claims responsibly, particularly for pre-existing or recently diagnosed conditions. Bajaj General Insurance policies typically include various waiting periods, such as an initial period, specific ailment periods, etc. for pre-existing diseases. The actual duration varies by plan & the diesease.

chunks.text: Yes, Bajaj General Insurance understands the growing preference for diverse healthcare approaches among Indians. chunks.text: OPD cover in health insurance supports expenses like doctor consultations, diagnostic tests, and medicines without hospitalisation. chunks.text: Yes, you can cancel your existing health insurance for a refund and consider switching to a reliable insurer like Bajaj General Insurance. Post free-look, a pro-rata refund for the unexpired term might be available, as per your current insurer's specific terms.
